extracted.intended_audience: math creators and community members interested in submitting explainer videos or written math exposition to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoMEπ)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a community-driven math exposition (video or written explainer) for SoMEπ, participate in the peer-review system, and engage with the community around the deadline. The event emphasizes mutual encouragement and growth rather than prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry format — "video or written math explainer"
rubrics_metrics.description: You would submit an entry, say a video or written math explainer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will be accepted via the SoME site (https://some.3b1b.co) in the weeks before the deadline. The phrasing 'say a video or written math explainer' indicates flexibility in medium but signals that the target is expository mathematics content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline compliance — shared deadline advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline is August 18th at 11:59 PM (UTC-12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the main benefits of the event is having a shared deadline; submit by the stated time to participate in the peer-review window and community timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in peer review — "period when everyone's work gets reviewed by peers"
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting, you join the peer review system to have a few other entries delivered to you for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer-review step produces an ordered list of entries and is central to the event's value. Participants are expected to both give and receive feedback; this mutual review is what spurs exposure and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-prizes / decentralized ranking — "no prizes, no winner selection"
rubrics_metrics.description: SoMEπ will be decentralized: there will be no prizes and no winner selection; the ordered list produced by peer review has no stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success is reframed to focus on 'internal sense of pride and growth' rather than final placement. Organizers may signal-boost the list, but there are no official rewards attached to rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community governance — policies decided by community
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about policies are ultimately up to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers (Grant, James, Fred) are willing to hand off systems and facilitation to community members. Join the SoME discord and ping the @organizer role with specific questions to engage in governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-in promotion / featuring — signal-boosting and creator curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers may do something to signal-boost the peer-review list, and other creators could optionally choose and feature their favorite entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no imposed promotion scheme; authors and community members can choose to highlight favorites, and the original organizers may amplify the list at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational responsibility — community oversight of peer-review system
rubrics_metrics.description: To replicate past benefits, the community should take responsibility for overseeing the peer review process and for doing needed development/bug fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A custom system from past years exists and could be handed off; Fred is available to do added development to fix issues, but success requires enough community members comfortable with stewardship and active management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goals / success criteria — mutual encouragement and growth
rubrics_metrics.description: The event emphasizes mutual encouragement and the internal sense of pride and growth from authors more than external rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success less by placement and more by participant experience: engagement in peer feedback, personal development as an explainer, and community interaction.
